newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific seeks to acquire Pennzoil.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific seeks to acquire Pennzoil.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc said early Monday it had renewed its attempt to acquire Pennzoil Co after its previous advances were rebuffed, offering a two-step cash and stock transaction valued at about $6.4 billion.
Union Pacific said the first step was a cash tender offer for 50.1 percent of Pennzoil's shares, followed by a tax-free exchange of shares for the remaining 49.9 percent.
The proposed transaction is valued at $84 per Pennzoil share, which closed Friday down 1/8 at 59-5/8 a share.

"We believe that the merger of UPR and Pennzoil will create the premier independent exploration and production company in the U.S.," Union Pacific chairman and chief executive Jack Messman said in a statement. "Driven by UPR's proven ability to drill and develop oil and gas properties quickly and efficiently, we are confident that UPR will create growth and value well beyond what Pennzoil can achieve on its own."
Union Pacific said the combined company would lead the industry in a number of performance measures, including drilling activity, production and cash flow.
The company said the deal would offer an immediate and ongoing accretion to its cash flow per share. However, it is expected to have a near-term dilutive effect on earnings per share.
In the first step of the transaction, a Union Pacific subsidiary is offering to acquire 50.1 percent of Pennzoil's common shares in a cash tender offer starting today.

In the second step, each remaining Pennzoil share will be exchanged for a number of Union Pacific shares, determined, within a pricing collar of $25 to $30, by dividing $84 by the average of the closing prices of Union Pacific common stock for the 20 consecutive trading days ending five days prior to the meeting of Pennzoil shareholders called for the purpose of voting on the proposed merger.
In the event that the Union Pacific exchange ratio price is less than $25 or greater than $30, the exchange ratio will be fixed at 3.36 shares, or 2.80 shares, respectively, it said.

The transaction must be approved by Union Pacific and Pennzoil shareholders. The transaction is not conditioned upon financing and the cash tender offer will be financed by Union Pacific with bank borrowings, it said.

Union Pacific's Messman has sent a letter to Pennzoil chairman and chief executive James Pate, whom the company said in a statement has "repeatedly rebuffed UPR's efforts to have any serious discussion about a possible transaction."
"These two companies belong together," Messman said in the letter.
Messman's letter also mentioned that Pate in 1995 proposed a merger with UPR, when it was a subsidiary of Union Pacific Corp.
Messman's letter also questioned Pate's view, contained in a May 8, 1997, letter to Messman, that a merger somehow no longer made sense, the company said.

"We do not understand," Messman wrote, "why you believed that two years ago, when Pennzoil faced particularly severe problems, it was in a better position than it is now to merge with UPR and form the premier independent E&P company. In fact, we believe that today the benefits from a combination would come even more quickly."
Union Pacific Resources said it sought a friendly merger but that its advances were repeatedly rebuffed.

"Your continued refusal to discuss the rationale or valuation of a transaction has left us with no choice but to present our offer directly to Pennzoil shareholders," Messman wrote. "While we are still prepared to discuss a friendly transaction, the UPR board of directors strongly supports pursuing a business combination now."
